key_insight: OptiPESS uses geometry-aware Hamiltonian similarity to adapt compute budgets across related quantum-classical workloads rather than optimizing every instance with fixed resources.
engineering_relevance: Built on CUDA-Q, the runtime combines adaptive scheduling with persistent multi-GPU execution to reduce evaluation costs and wall-time while maintaining baseline accuracy.
method: Align Hamiltonians and classify Pauli terms to expose cross-instance structure.
Use the Locality-Occupancy-Variance (LOV) metric to estimate Hamiltonian similarity.
Allocate iteration and shot budgets, selecting instances to skip, quick-solve, or fully optimize.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 78.3% fewer classical and quantum evaluations, up to 74.8% lower wall-time, and near-linear multi-GPU scaling while maintaining baseline accuracy.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify benchmark coverage or accuracy tolerances, leaving generalization beyond the evaluated workloads uncertain.
paper_title: A GPU-Accelerated and Geometry-Aware Quantum-Classical Framework for Optimized PES Scans with CUDA-Q
